title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 7: crown of ministry vs heavenly glory — alternate reading first
pass_a_gloss: I answer: these words can with no less probability be fitted to the crown of ministry than to the crown of heavenly glory, in this sense: Hold what you have — that is, exercise the episcopal office constantly and diligently; lest another take your crown — that is, lest, if you show yourself negligent, another, you being rejected, be put in your place. But because the same words can not inconveniently, and are accustomed by many to be referred to the crown of heavenly glory, that sense being admitted, we reply.
pass_b_english: Reply: the words fit the crown of ministry at least as well as heavenly glory — "Hold what you have" as keep the bishop's office steadily and carefully; "lest another take your crown" as lest, if you prove negligent, someone else is put in your place after you are set aside. Still, many read them of the heavenly crown without strain. Take that sense, and we answer as follows.
source_text: Respondeo, haec verba non minore probabilitate ad coronam ministerii accommodari posse quam ad coronam caelestis gloriae, hoc nimirum sensu; Tene quod habes, id est, Episcopale officium constanter & diligenter exerce: ne alius accipiat coronam tuam, hoc est, ne, si tu negligentem te ostenderis, alius, te rejecto, in locum tuum sufficiatur. Sed quia eadem verba possunt haud incommode, & solent a multis, ad coronam caelestis gloriae referri, hoc sensu admisso, respondemus.
